$description: Ergo Light — tool-agnostic design tokens. Layer 1 (primitive ramps) + Layer 2 (semantic roles). Adapters in theme/generate.py translate semantic tokens into per-tool files; no tool reads this file directly. Ramps rebuilt in OKLCH: an eased perceptual L* ladder (steps compress toward the light end so background tints get more resolution), a single locked hue per ramp, and one shared chroma ceiling (~0.061 across the ink steps 300-700) so every accent carries equal weight. Light-end steps 100/200 sit on a three-tier tint scale — whisper ~1.13:1, standard ~1.30:1, strong ~1.55:1 vs paper — so state washes read across displays, not just calibrated ones; those wash steps are additionally desaturated (C≈0.026, amber's slightly higher at ~0.022-0.040 so warm wheat stays clean not olive) so they read as quiet tinted paper rather than colour blocks (see primitive.$description for the two-regime chroma model). Direction: calm neutral paper (one shared bg), soft ink ~10:1, muted 'dusty' accents (uniform low chroma, ~4.9:1 at the .600 step), very soft near-neutral background tints.

primitive.$description: Layer 1 — raw color ramps, hue + lightness (50 lightest, 900 darkest). Eased in perceptual L* (steps compress toward the light end) with a single locked hue. TWO CHROMA REGIMES by design: light steps (50-200) are near-neutral background tints (C≈0.008-0.026 — softened so state washes read as quiet tinted paper, not colour blocks), then chroma steps up to a normal 'ink' plateau (C≈0.06) across 300-700. Within that plateau the roles split by lightness, not chroma: the light end (300, L≈0.82) is the strong background 'pop' tier — selection, active search, diff word-emph — while the AA-readable foregrounds live at the dark end (600-700, ~4.9-7.7:1 on paper). 300 is NOT a foreground step (~1.5:1); it only shares the plateau's chroma so a strong-tier background carries the same hue weight as an accent. The 200→300 chroma jump (~+0.034) is intentional, not a break — backgrounds stay quiet, foregrounds carry hue; the seam lands exactly on the wash→pop boundary. Amber's light end sits slightly above the other tints' chroma (~0.022-0.040, not the former ~2x) and is rotated warmer to ~74-78° because a desaturated ~90° yellow greys to dirty olive — enough to read as clean warm wheat without shouting. Meaningless on their own; semantic tokens give them roles.

gray.$description: Neutral grey (hue stripped, C*≈0) — every surface, border, and ink tone. Was 'barely-warm' but the warm hue put a yellow film over the whole editor; neutralised at identical lightness so all contrasts hold. base (50) is the single shared environment background for nvim, terminal and zellij; a soft off-white (not stark) so it reads calm, not glary.

red.$description: Errors, deletions, and the warm mode-accent. Hue locked to ~18° (clean crimson), NOT the ~29° red-orange the ramp used to sit at. Note ~29° IS pure sRGB red — the ramp wasn't mis-hued; the problem is that a dark, low-chroma WARM colour reads as 'brick/brown' regardless of hue (brown is just dark desaturated orange). Rotating to ~18° moves the mid-dark steps across a colour-NAMING boundary: the green and blue channels equalise (e.g. 600 #87595A, G≈B) so the orange cast drops out and the dark steps read as 'wine/maroon' — still named red — instead of brick, which is named brown. Held L* and chroma per-step (only H changed) so every contrast ratio and the add/delete CVD lightness offset are untouched; verified add-vs-delete stays ΔE≈4.6 under deuteranopia. Target 18° is deliberately the crossover point — far enough to kill the brown cast, not so far it tips into rose/pink (that starts ~15° and below). Light steps read as clean soft rose (git-standard deletion tint), dark steps as clean dark red.

amber.$description: Warm gold ramp — comment washes (light) and warnings (dark). (diff-change moved off amber to blue, and search moved off amber to cyan; amber's light end is now a single 'attention' family — comment band + TODO markers — not a grab-bag of unrelated roles. Both transient interactive states now live on cool hues instead: selection=violet, search=cyan.) Light steps are pinned to ~74-78° (warm wheat), NOT pure yellow ~90°: a desaturated 90° yellow greys toward dirty olive/khaki, so the softened light-end tints are rotated warmer to read as clean wheat/cream. The wash steps (100-300) were de-chroma'd toward the other ramps' tint budget (C≈0.022-0.040, down from a former ~2x) so amber reads as quiet warm paper rather than a saturated gold block on the highest-traffic surface (the comment band). It still sits a touch above the neutral ~0.026 tint chroma — warm wheat needs slightly more chroma than green/blue/red to stay clean rather than muddy grey — but no longer overpowers them. The whole ramp runs a single monotonic wheat->gold hue path (~78° light to ~72° gold dark, ~6° total spread); dark steps (400-900) carry the gold end for warning/terminal foregrounds. Hue was corrected to this smooth ease from a prior hand-authored state where step 400 drifted to ~84° (a yellow spike mid-ramp); the fix rotated hue only, holding each step's L* and chroma so no contrast or accent-weight changed.

blue.$description: Info, links, functions, and calm structural-content surfaces — doc backgrounds and diff.change ('modified'). Blue backgrounds all mean the same neutral thing (a quiet, PERSISTENT informational/structural surface). Interactive selection and matching-ref highlights (transient, cursor-driven) deliberately live on VIOLET, not blue. Blue's light tiers now carry: doc.50 (doc/quote background) and the diff pair change.100 (changed line) / changeText.200 (changed word). change.100 sits at the whisper tier ABOVE diff.add (green.200) on purpose — it puts the modified-line band a lightness step off additions so add-vs-change survives red-green CVD (see semantic.diff.change); changeText.200 is one step darker, the intentional word-emphasis anchor (mirrors add/addText). doc and diffs don't co-occur in one buffer, and the change/changeText pair is a deliberate emphasis step, not a collision — so blue never recreates amber's old overload (conflicting urgencies double-booked on one step). blue = persistent content, violet = live selection.

cyan.$description: Cyan ramp — terminal cyan channel (dark end, .600) AND editor search highlights (light end, 300/400). Two non-overlapping regimes on one otherwise-unused hue. Search took cyan so it would sit clear of the warm comment band (amber) and read as its own transient state, parallel to selection on violet — see semantic.search.soft. cyan.300 = all-matches band, cyan.400 = current match; both light/pop-tier, distinct buffer from the .600 terminal foreground.

violet.$description: Blue-violet — constants (dark end, .700) and interactive selection (light end, 100/300). Two non-overlapping regimes on one hue: the .700 foreground names constants in code, while the 100/300 washes are the reserved 'live selection' surfaces (selection.match, selection.primary) — a different buffer and a different step, so they never collide. Violet carries selection so blue can mean only persistent content/structure; see semantic.selection.primary for the overload-resolution rationale.

alert.$description: OFF-RAMP alarm red — the ONE place the two-regime chroma model is broken on purpose. Every other ink step is pinned to the ~0.061 ceiling so 'every accent carries equal weight'; that uniformity is exactly what lets a single high-chroma element pop pre-attentively (a saturation feature-singleton). alert.fg sits at C≈0.207 — ~3.4x the ceiling — so an error is the only saturated thing on screen and the eye finds it before it consciously looks. NOT on the eased L* ladder and NOT a ramp (a single named fg, not numeric steps) precisely so nobody mistakes it for a tunable accent: it is the reserved 'demands action' dimension, used by error diagnostics only. #CE1F1F (L≈0.55, h≈28 clean alarm red not the ramp's 18° wine) is AA on paper (4.93:1) so the sign glyph and bold virtual text read; the high chroma + the undercurl SHAPE make it CVD-robust (chroma magnitude and shape survive red-green deficiency where hue alone would not). Applied as foreground only — undercurl, bold sign glyph, bold virtual text, :messages errors — no fill: the saturation IS the singleton, a background block just read as a clunky box. Warnings deliberately stay on the muted amber ceiling, one tier down, so the alert axis is ordered: error shouts, warning speaks, info/hint whisper.

semantic.$description: Layer 2 — roles in the Ergo Light language. Tool-agnostic: these describe meaning (a surface, an error, a string), never a tool. Every value is an alias into a primitive ramp so the whole system re-tunes from Layer 1.

base.$description: shared background for editor, terminal and zellij — soft neutral paper

cursorline.$description: current-line highlight — stepped to gray.200 so it is actually visible on paper

popup.$description: popup / telescope bg — one step off base so it reads as a layer, not just a border

primary.$description: body text / default fg — soft neutral dark (~10:1), calm not harsh

muted.$description: hints, line numbers, muted UI (comments use comment.fg)

constant.$description: constants, numbers, booleans — dropped one step from violet.600 so a lightness cue survives the blue↔violet hue collapse under deuteranopia/protanopia (function stays at blue.600; without the offset the two are indistinguishable for red-green CVD)

link.$description: links / urls — dropped to blue.800 so constant can stay vivid at violet.700 without the two colliding under CVD (link and constant share a hue axis but never the same buffer)

error.$description: errors — darkest red, 2 steps below the warm mode-accent so the two never read alike

alert.$description: The 'demands action' tier — error only, kept separate from status.error so terminal/delta/zellij red stays muted (status.error = red.700, the calm ANSI-side red) while the editor's error MARK shouts. This is the chroma-singleton fix for a uniform-chroma palette: because nothing else is saturated, error needs only to break the ceiling to pop, not to be loud everywhere. One lever, error-scoped: the saturated undercurl / sign glyph / bold virtual-text colour (foreground only — no fill). Warnings stay on amber one tier down — the axis is ordered, not flattened.

fg.$description: loud error foreground — undercurl, bold sign glyph, inline virtual text, :messages errors

primary.$description: active selection — VIOLET, not blue. Moved off blue.300 to resolve blue's light-tier overload: blue had consumed all four of its pop/wash steps (50 doc, 100 match, 200 diff.change, 300 selection), leaving no gap between a transient interactive state (selection) and a persistent content state (diff.change) that can co-occur. Violet reserves a hue for 'your live selection', splitting the axis cleanly: blue = persistent content/structure, violet = interactive selection. Still strong-tier (violet.300, ~1.5:1) so it separates from the neutral current-line highlight (cursorline = gray.200; ΔE≈8.3, matching the old blue.300's 8.2 — the collision that pushed selection off gray stays solved). Distinct from diff.change (now blue.100, a lighter whisper tier; selection is darker and violet): ΔE≈11.3, holding ≈11.2–11.4 under deuteranopia/protanopia, so a selection inside a changed line reads clearly. Violet's light tiers were previously unused (violet only appeared as a foreground, constant at .700, a different buffer/step), so no new conflict. Dark text stays readable (~6.7:1). A selection is a transient interactive state meant to be seen, so it carries ink-tier chroma, not quiet wash chroma.

match.$description: matched pair / reference — moved to violet.100 with selection.primary. Bracket-match and reference highlights track the cursor (they move as you move), so they belong to the interactive/violet family, not the structural/blue one. Keeping the selection pair on a single hue vacated blue.100 — which diff.change then took (change=blue.100) to build the add>change>delete lightness ladder — leaving blue's light tiers as persistent content plus that one diff pair (doc.50; change.100/changeText.200), none of which co-occur as a collision.

soft.$description: search match bg — moved to CYAN (an otherwise editor-unused hue), off amber. On amber.300 the all-matches highlight sat one step from comment.bg (amber.200): both warm wheat washes, ~5.5 dE / ~1.2:1 apart, so a match landing inside a comment nearly vanished. cyan.300 clears the comment band decisively (dE~10.3, deut ~9.0) while holding the same strong/'pop' presence search wants (~1.54:1 on paper, matching amber.300's old ~1.58). This also makes the interactive-state hues symmetric: selection=violet, search=cyan, each a dedicated cool hue off the content hues, and it frees amber to mean one thing (comment band + TODO markers + warnings). ONE residual: search.soft (cyan.300) and selection (violet.300) both sit at L~0.82, so an all-matches band overlapping a selection collapses to dE~2.4 under deuteranopia. Low severity: transient-vs-transient (not content), fine in normal vision (dE~8.1), and the CURRENT match (search.active, cyan.400) stays strongly separated from selection (dE~13.8). Dark text on cyan.300 ~7.0:1.

active.$description: current search / incsearch — one step above search.soft (cyan.400) so the match under the cursor out-reads the other matches (dE~11 from search.soft). Dark text stays AA-readable on it (~4.7:1), matching the old amber.400's ~4.6:1.

fg.$description: comment foreground — aliased to text.secondary (same weight); comments are signal, meant to be read

bg.$description: normal comment band — stepped up from amber.100 (whisper, ~1.13:1, which faded to nothing on uncalibrated panels) to amber.200 (standard, ~1.32:1) so the warm band is perceptible while staying a low-chroma wheat wash (C~0.033), not a gold block. This is a QUIET band by measurement, not a loud one: 1.32:1 is the standard-wash tier, barely above the whisper it replaced. The prominence comments get in this theme comes almost entirely from the FOREGROUND weight (comment.fg = text.secondary, ~7.5:1 — comments read as strong as secondary UI text), not from the fill; the band's job is just to warm the region so the eye groups it, without shouting. Sole owner of amber.200 (diff.change lives on blue), so it never shares a step with another role.

high.$description: high-priority comment markers (TODO/FIXME/WARNING/NOTE) — amber.300 (strong tier), one step above the normal comment band (amber.200) so a marker out-reads the surrounding comments. Now the SOLE amber pop-tier role: search left amber for cyan, so amber.300 no longer collides with a search highlight. Amber's light end is a single coherent family — comment band (200), markers (300) — both warm 'this is annotation', differing only by priority.

add.$description: added lines — standard-tier tint (~1.31:1 on paper) so the wash reads across displays, not just calibrated ones. Kept a light wash step while diff.delete sits one tier darker; see diff.delete for why the pair is intentionally asymmetric (CVD).

addText.$description: word-level emphasis inside an added line (delta plus-emph / nvim DiffText) — one step above the line tint (strong tier) so the changed word out-reads the line, and lighter than diff.deleteText so add/delete word-patches separate by lightness under CVD.

change.$description: changed/modified lines (nvim DiffChange) — BLUE, not amber, and stepped to the WHISPER tier (blue.100) so the fill carries its own signal. Two problems drove this. (1) De-collision: amber.200 was double-booked as both this and comment.bg; comment.bg is now amber.200's sole owner. (2) CVD lightness: add=green.200 and the former change=blue.200 were near-isoluminant (ΔL≈0), so add-vs-change collapsed to ΔE≈3.85 under deuteranopia — hue on the CVD-preserved blue↔yellow axis was technically intact but too low-chroma (C≈0.026) to do the work, leaving the +/- gutter glyph as the only real cue. Dropping change to blue.100 (L≈0.92) lifts it ABOVE add (green.200, L≈0.87), which sits above delete (red.300, L≈0.82): a clean monotonic lightness ladder change>add>delete where every diff state separates by lightness alone (add/change now ΔE≈5.5 deut, ≈5.9 normal). Cost: blue.100 is a faint band (~1.14:1 on paper) — deliberately calm for 'neutral modification', with the changed WORD (changeText, blue.200) carrying the visible anchor. Git-standard add/delete keep mint/rose, changed is the quiet blue — matching VS Code's gutter (add=green / modified=blue / delete=red). Dark text ~9.4:1.

changeText.$description: word-level emphasis inside a changed line (nvim DiffText) — blue.200, now one step ABOVE the change line (blue.100). Previously change and changeText were both blue.200 (flat); dropping the line to blue.100 for the add/change lightness ladder turns this into a genuine word-patch, mirroring add/addText (line at N, word at N+1). It gives the faint change band a visible anchor exactly on the changed span (~1.31:1 vs paper, dark text ~8.2:1) without making the whole line loud.

delete.$description: deleted lines — stepped one tier ABOVE diff.add (add=green.200 L≈0.87; delete=red.300 L≈0.82) on purpose. Because the ramp couples lightness and chroma, add (a light wash step) and delete (an ink step) can only separate in lightness by also separating in chroma — so deletions read slightly stronger and warmer than additions. That asymmetry is the point: add/delete are the classic red-green isoluminant pair, the exact axis deuteranopia/protanopia collapses; at the same step they sat at ΔL≈0.012 (indistinguishable under CVD), now ΔL≈0.053. The gutter +/- signs (always present in delta/nvim/git) remain the primary cue; this lightness offset is the color-only backstop.

deleteText.$description: word-level emphasis inside a deleted line (delta minus-emph) — one step below diff.addText (addText=green.300 L≈0.82; deleteText=red.400 L≈0.71, ΔL≈0.111) so the changed word is CVD-separable from an added word by lightness, not hue alone. Deeper than the delete line so the word still pops within its own line.

primary.$description: primary cursor block — kept near-black so the caret stays easy to spot

terminal.$description: The ANSI palette is a role a terminal plays, not a tool. Muted on purpose vs the editor accents. The 'white' channels are a hard light-theme constraint, not a loose choice: color 15 (bright white) must stay LIGHTER than color 7 (white) to preserve ANSI ordering, and on light paper 'lighter than the lightest AA-passing grey' is by definition sub-AA — so bright.white CANNOT reach AA as body text without breaking the ordering. gray.500 (3.4:1, AA-large) is therefore the provable optimum for bright.white, and white=gray.600 (5.1:1, AA) is as light as color 7 can go while passing AA. This only bites apps that explicitly paint body text in ANSI 7/15; the terminal's DEFAULT foreground is text.primary (gray.800, ~10.7:1), so ordinary uncoloured output is never affected.
